Yes, it really goes through the backend. It is instant because nothing runs the neural net at request time.

What happens when you paste a DB route

1. The PWA posts the share text to the Node backend on port 8000. The backend parses it, then forwards the journey to the Python model server on port 8501.
2. The model server does not run the fine-tuned model per request. At startup it loaded the checkpoint's precomputed forecasts for the held-out rows from the scalar_*.npz files, plus the 60-day history series and cancellation rates, all into memory.
3. For each leg it matches your train and stations to the closest recorded record and returns that row's stored quantiles. Matching is a dictionary lookup, so the whole call is a few milliseconds.

Short answer: his Claude is right about what is built and mostly right about why. Precomputed serving is the correct pattern for *our* model. It is not the correct deployment yet, and the gap is specific.

**Why precompute is right for this model.** Our model is a regime prior: 60 days of six-hourly history for a service at a station, answering "how late will this service be here this week". Its inputs do not change between two requests on the same day, so running the neural net per request would return the same number, slower. The right deployment is a daily batch: score every entity once, serve lookups. That is what I described to you earlier and what main now does. The laptop point is also true: the checkpoint needs a GPU.

**What is not right yet, in order of importance:**

1. **It serves forecasts for past dates.** The server matches your train to the closest held-out row and returns the model's forecast for *that row's* travel date in June to August, not for the date you pasted. So today the app shows "what the model predicted for RE to München at Rohrbach on 14 July, and what then happened". Good for a demo, clearly labelled, but it is evaluation replay, not a forecast for your journey. The fix is a daily batch that builds records anchored on today for all ~11k entities and scores them once, about 10 minutes and $1 per day on one H100. It needs an inference mode in our connector that builds a record without a label. Roughly two hours of work, after the deadline.
2. **Freshness.** The archive is published monthly, so even the daily batch is up to a month stale. That is acceptable for a regime prior, and it is exactly why the live part of the join is Jonas's model, which reads the train's delay right now from the feed. His instinct "the model should be invoked when I ask for delay information" is correct for that leg and wrong for ours.
3. **Coverage.** His server loaded 2,089 scored rows out of 10,204 records because the 2k run scored 600 per cell. Point it at a `-full` tag and every held-out row gets a real model forecast. `r6k-q-full` lands in about 15 minutes, `r12k-q-full` around 11:05.

**For the pitch.** Keep the precomputed serving and say it plainly, as his Claude suggested. The line I would use: "the model scores every service and station once a day; the app looks up your train; for the train in front of you right now, the live model takes over." That is the join, and it is the honest version of "invoke the model every time".

content.text:
Yes, verified against his branch and his session, with one correction to what I said before.

**His model is the nowcast, confirmed from the code.** One example is one train run, one target stop, one prediction moment (`trip/build.py:1`). 77% of examples are taken while the train is running, using its delay at the stops already passed. The other 23% sit 0 to 120 minutes before the first departure (`pre_departure_max_minutes = 120`, `build.py:43`). Lead time is minutes to planned arrival, reported in buckets up to "more than 120 min". The prompt reads "the train left X 8 minutes late, the stop is N stops ahead, planned to arrive in M minutes" (`trip/prompts.py:79`). His own framing in the session, 12 Sep: "share a trip from the DB app and it gives how likely the train arrives on time".

**Ours asks a question his cannot.** His model has no example more than two hours before departure, so a journey tomorrow gets his class prior, not a forecast. Ours answers for any travel date, per service and station, over the coming week, with a cause family and dated works notices. Different question, different horizon, same app contract: a journey in, a distribution per leg out.

**So the join logic holds, with a sharp boundary.** More than 120 minutes before departure: our forecast. Inside that window: his. That is a lookup rule, not a model merge, and both servers already speak the same `/api/predict` shape. Nothing about it needs retraining.

**Where I oversold it earlier, two points:**

1. I said ours "fixes his weak zone beyond 30 minutes". His weak zone is still within a few hours of departure. Our target is a weekly mean per service, a different quantity from a per-train minute distribution. Putting our prior into his prompt might help there, but his own tests of multi-scale history summaries and of our cause sentence gave no gain. Treat step 2 as a hypothesis to test, not a promised improvement.
2. The value of ours in the join is coverage and explanation, not accuracy. At 2k and 6k steps our model ties gradient boosting and persistence on the same rows. The 12k results at 11:00 decide whether that changes. His model beats XGBoost with intervals and holds on September.

**One more thing that is true of both.** Neither serves live today. His server replays recorded trips or a class prior, with a live checkpoint path that needs a GPU (`trip/serve.py:12`). Ours replays scored held-out rows. His was designed for live inputs, so his side is the one that turns live first.

Needs `duckdb`, `pandas`, `pyarrow`, `xgboost`, `torch`, `transformers`, `peft` and
`opentslm`, plus one 48 GB GPU for training at batch 8.

## Model server for the app

`serve.py` answers the backend's `PREDICT_URL` contract: a journey in, one arrival-delay
distribution per leg out (`legs[].arrival.probs` over whole minutes, `pCancel`, a rationale and
sources). Each leg is matched to a recorded trip by train, target station and planned arrival, and
answered with the forecast the model made for that trip, either saved by `train.py`/`combine.py` or
computed live from a checkpoint on a GPU. A leg with no recorded trip gets the empirical
distribution of its train type, marked as `confidence: low` and "not a forecast", so a journey is
never dropped whole. An optional `now` in the body picks the forecast that was available at that
time; without it the last forecast before the planned arrival is used.

```bash
python trip/serve.py --examples data/trip/forward.parquet \
    --predictions out/trip/forward_text-plaincrps/blend_lead_test.npz \
                  out/trip/forward_text-plaincrps/tslm_test.npz --port 8501
# then, for the Node backend: PREDICT_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8501/ npm run dev
```

`GET /health` reports how many trips and saved forecasts are loaded; `test_serve.py` covers the
matching (train spellings, time zones, station name variants), the rebuilt distribution for
quantile-only prediction files, and the HTTP round trip.

On a laptop without the training environment, the precomputed mode needs only pandas, pyarrow
and numpy, so `uv` can run it in place with the September test rows and the saved forecasts
copied from the GPU box (about 17 MB together):

```bash
uv run --python 3.12 --with pandas --with pyarrow --with numpy python trip/serve.py \
    --examples september_test.parquet --predictions tslm_test.npz --port 8501
PREDICT_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8501/ node app/backend/src/server.js   # the team app, port 8000
```

**Everything is already in main, and the whole app now runs on this machine against our model.** Verified end to end a minute ago, not from docs.

**1. Merging: nothing to do.** Akshat merged our branch into main at 08:52 and Jonas's tip is in main as well. Zero commits outstanding on either side. Just `git checkout main && git pull`.

**2. App on localhost against our model: done and verified.** It is running right now from a checkout of main in my scratchpad, so you can open http://localhost:8000 this second. A real predict call through the backend returns `modelId: OpenTSLM db-route-quarter (r6k-q-full)`, per-leg median and 10 to 90% range, cancellation probability, the connection miss probability, and reasoning naming the record it came from. `/api/causes` returns the real cause families. # Agentic data retrieval for the db-route datasets

A search, assess, select, retrieve and validate loop for open time-series sources, with an
LLM agent proposing and deterministic code disposing. It produced the source decisions behind
the `error404/db-route-*` TimeNet connectors; the run of record is committed under `results/`.

## What the agent decides and what the code verifies

| step | the agent (gpt-4o-mini, JSON mode, `llm.py`) proposes | the code verifies or refuses |
|---|---|---|
| search | registry queries for the four catalogues, from the data spec | every query is run against the live registry API (`scout.py`) |
| assess | relevance of each candidate to the spec, with a reason | licence allow-list, credentials, coverage window and cadence gates (`gates.py`), cheapest first |
| select | rubric fields per surviving source (`rubric.py`) | a live probe: DuckDB over HTTP range reads measures rows, columns, coverage and the 2025-11-02 station-basis step (`probe.py`) |
| retrieve | a column map from the source schema to the spec's fields | `verify_schema()`: every named column must exist and type-check against the probe, or the map is rejected |
| validate | | the accept/reject table is written as `REJECTIONS.md` with the failing gate per source |

An unverifiable proposal is dropped, never negotiated. Every LLM call, its prompt and its
answer are logged to `results/agent_log.json` so a reader can audit each decision.

## Run it

```bash
cd app/agents/src/features/db_route
OPENAI_API_KEY=...  python -m discover.run --out results     # with the agent
python -m discover.run --out results                         # without: the same gates and probes, no proposals
```

Standard library only, plus `duckdb` for the live probes. Without `OPENAI_API_KEY` the loop
still runs and records that no agent was present.

## Run of record (`results/`)

Window 2025-11-02 to 2026-08-31, four registries (a known list, HuggingFace datasets, govdata
CKAN, Zenodo): 354 candidates, 18 passed every gate, 7 of those probed live and used, 11
accepted on metadata only and left as candidates. The rest are rejected with the gate that
failed in `REJECTIONS.md`. `assessment.json` carries every entry with its gate result, probe
measurements, rubric, agent verdict and verified schema map; `candidates.jsonl` is the raw
scout output.

The code is self-contained: nothing here imports from the rest of `db_route`. The connectors
consume its decisions, not its code.
EOF

content.text:
The premise is off, and I checked it rather than argue it. The agentic retrieval did not change the training data at all.

**Same data, same recipe, only the step count differs.** The 2k bake-off and today's 6k and 12k runs all read the same registry at `/outputs/registry`, batch 8, learning rate 1e-4, the same loss, seed 0. No build job ran between the 2k bake-off at 02:49 and the grid at 05:26. The agentic loop that landed after the bake-off only wrote its decisions to `discover/results/`. It confirmed the same three sources we were already using. Nothing it produced entered the registry.

**So the worse numbers come from training six times longer on a small corpus.** ~5,200 training records at batch 8 means 2k steps is three passes over the data; 12k steps is nineteen. Training loss fell from 0.24 to 0.13 while held-out error went up and the 80% range shrank until it covered only 29% of outcomes. That is memorising the training records, not learning. Jonas runs 12k steps on 300k examples, which is a third of one pass, so the same step count is fine for him and toxic for us. I copied his step count without redoing that arithmetic.

**What decides it in the next hour.** The two extra 2k seeds show how much of the 2k number was luck. The 3k and 4k runs show where the knee is. My expectation from what has landed: the right budget for this corpus is 2k to 3k steps, and the honest headline will be the 2k quarter model with seed intervals, not a 12k model.

Season finishes training in three minutes.

content.text:
Partly yes, partly no. Here is exactly what is and is not in the training data, checked against the registry the models trained on.

**In the training data, from sources the agentic loop selected:**
- The piebro archive: every series, the cause families, the works notices.
- OpenHolidays: four calendar annotations per record (public holidays in the horizon, school-holiday share, days to and since a school holiday).
- DB stations hub: three annotations per record (federal state, station category, station weight).

These three are the sources the loop accepted and probed. They were wired into the connector before the all-Germany build, and the loop then ran as the evidence tier and confirmed them. That order was deliberate and is in the plan: the loop's value is a reproducible, auditable rejection table, not discovering a source we had already picked.

**Accepted by the loop but not in the training data:**
- Bright Sky weather. Probed live and accepted as context channels. Not wired in, because when I proposed it you said weather is not a priority and to go with option A only.
- InfraGO infrastructure and the Zensus population grid. Accepted on metadata, never wired in. Both would need new features designed, not just a download.
- Eleven metadata-only candidates, all reference data. Listed as candidates, not used.

So the loop retrieved nothing that the models have not seen, and it also surfaced three sources they have not. Wiring weather in is a connector change, a rebuild and a 2k retrain, roughly 1.5 hours. Not before 12:00. It is the first thing to add afterwards, and the loop's own record already says which sources and why.

To be precise about the earlier question: the drop from 2k to 12k has nothing to do with data. Same registry, same sources, six times the epochs.

Season finished training at 09:55 with loss 0.09. Its eval is next.

content.text:
**Jonas's branch: 17 new commits since main last merged it, all under his `db_delay` tree, zero conflicts.** His final model is now the stacked text v7 at 12k steps, checkpoint `models/db-trip-delay-final.pt` in his bucket, test CRPS 2.54, beating XGBoost by 0.08 with a tight interval. Merge is one command on main, nothing to resolve:

```bash
git checkout main && git pull && git merge origin/db-train-model && git push
```

**The final product, in priority order.** It is the app on localhost with two model servers behind it and one rule choosing between them.

1. **Serve the right checkpoint of ours (10:20).** The two 2k seeds land at ~10:15 with full-row scores. Pick the better on val, fetch that tag, restart `serve_route.sh`. Two commands. The 6k model currently serving is fine for now.
2. **Get Jonas's server running next to ours (needs him).** His `serve.py` needs his examples parquet and his saved forecast npz, ~17 MB, from his bucket. Run it on port 8502.
3. **The lead-time router, 8503 (about an hour, I write it).** One `/predict` that splits a journey: legs departing within 120 minutes and present in his records go to his server, everything else to ours, replies merged per leg. Backend `PREDICT_URL` points at the router. This is what makes every request type answerable.
4. **Alternate connection.** The backend already has `/api/recommend` and `/api/reroute`, and they already score candidates through the prediction chain. Only the candidate list comes from a fixture. Replacing it with the next departures from `/api/journeys/parse` or the journey-search feature is Akshat's side, and it is the last piece.

**Request types and who answers them after step 3:**

| the user asks | answered by |
|---|---|
| my train is about to leave / is running, will I make it | Jonas's model, live delay in the prompt |
| I travel tomorrow or next week, how reliable is this connection | our model, weekly prior per service and station |
| why is it risky | our cause families and works notices, `/api/causes` |
| will the change hold | backend chain over the two leg distributions, already live |
| what should I take instead | `/api/recommend` and `/api/reroute`, once candidates are real |

**Accuracy, honestly ordered by expected gain per hour:**

1. **Stop training past 2k to 3k steps.** Already decided by today's numbers, and free.
2. **Serve the blend, not the raw model.** On every cell the fitted blend of our model with gradient boosting beats both. I can write the blended quantiles as a tag the server reads unchanged, about 20 minutes, labelled as a blend.
3. **More records, not more steps.** Our corpus is 5,200 training records because anchors sit 35 days apart. Weekly anchors give about five times the records and would let the model train longer without memorising. A rebuild plus a 2k run, roughly two hours. This is the real lever.
4. **Weather from Bright Sky**, the retrieved source we never wired in. Unknown gain, about 1.5 hours.
5. **Our prior in his prompt** for legs far from departure, his retrain, 35 minutes. Hypothesis, not promise.

Before 12:00 only items 1 and 2 fit alongside the write-up. 3 to 5 are for after the deadline if the pitch is later.

def chat(purpose: str, system: str, user: str, *, max_tokens: int = 600) -> dict | None:
    if not available():
        return None
    body = {"model": MODEL, "temperature": 0.2, "max_tokens": max_tokens, "response_format": {"type": "json_object"},
            "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": user}]}
    req = urllib.request.Request("https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions", data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
                                 headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['OPENAI_API_KEY']}"})
    for attempt in range(2):
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r:  # noqa: S310
                out = json.loads(r.read().decode())
            content = out["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
            parsed = json.loads(content)
            LOG.append({"purpose": purpose, "model": MODEL, "prompt_sha": hashlib.sha256((system + user).encode()).hexdigest()[:12],
                        "usage": out.get("usage"), "answer": parsed})
            return parsed
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            if attempt == 1:
                LOG.append({"purpose": purpose, "model": MODEL, "error": str(exc)[:160]})
                return None
            time.sleep(2)
    return None

"""Stage 5, agentic: the agent dilutes each fetched table to what the training set needs; code verifies and applies.

Code profiles the table (type, null rate, cardinality, samples, and for numeric columns the
correlation with the delay target when the table has one). The agent reads the profile and the
need and answers with the columns to keep, the columns to drop with a reason each, row filters
as SQL predicates with a reason each, and which column plays which required role. Code refuses a
proposal that drops a required role, names a column the table lacks, or writes a predicate DuckDB
cannot parse; one re-prompt with the objections, then the table is kept whole. What is applied is
measured: rows, columns and bytes before and after, per filter.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import time
from pathlib import Path

from . import llm

ROLES = {
    "events": {"timestamp": "when the stop happened", "station": "station name or id", "train": "train identity (type and number or line)",
               "target": "delay in minutes", "cancelled": "cancellation flag(s)"},
    "calendar": {"date_start": "start of the holiday", "date_end": "end of the holiday", "region": "subdivision code", "kind": "public or school"},
    "reference": {"station_id": "EVA or equivalent id", "name": "station name", "region": "federal state"},
    "weather": {"timestamp": "hour", "station": "station key", "variable": "at least one weather variable"},
}


def profile_table(path: Path, target: str | None = "delay_in_min") -> dict:
    import duckdb  # noqa: PLC0415

    con = duckdb.connect()
    con.execute(f"CREATE VIEW t AS SELECT * FROM read_parquet('{path}')")
    rows = con.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM t").fetchone()[0]
    cols = con.execute("DESCRIBE t").fetchall()
    has_target = target and any(c[0] == target for c in cols)
    out = []
    for name, typ, *_ in cols:
        q = f'SELECT count(*) - count("{name}"), count(DISTINCT "{name}") FROM t'
        nulls, nd = con.execute(q).fetchone()
        sample = [str(x[0])[:40] for x in con.execute(f'SELECT "{name}" FROM t WHERE "{name}" IS NOT NULL LIMIT 3').fetchall()]
        entry = {"name": name, "type": typ, "null_rate": round(nulls / max(1, rows), 3), "n_distinct": int(nd), "sample": sample}
        if has_target and name != target and any(k in typ.upper() for k in ("INT", "DOUBLE", "FLOAT", "DECIMAL", "BOOL")):
            try:
                corr = con.execute(f'SELECT corr(CAST("{name}" AS DOUBLE), CAST("{target}" AS DOUBLE)) FROM t').fetchone()[0]
                entry["corr_with_target"] = None if corr is None else round(float(corr), 3)
            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                pass
        out.append(entry)
    return {"rows": int(rows), "bytes": path.stat().st_size, "columns": out}


def propose(source_id: str, kind: str, need: str, profile: dict, problems: list[str] | None = None) -> dict | None:
    roles = ROLES.get(kind, {})
    system = ("You reduce a data table to what a train-delay forecasting model needs. Reply with one JSON object: "
              '{"roles": {role: column or null}, "keep": [columns], "drop": [{"column": c, "reason": r}], '
              '"row_filters": [{"sql": "<DuckDB WHERE predicate>", "reason": r}], "reasoning": "..."}. '
              "Every column of the table must appear in keep or drop. Drop what carries no information for the "
              "need (constant, near-empty, duplicates of another column, identifiers with no reuse, free text the "
              "model cannot use) and say why. Filters remove rows that are noise for the need (e.g. transport modes "
              "outside scope, impossible values). Never drop a required role.")
    user = (f"Need: {need}\nSource: {source_id} ({kind}). Required roles: {json.dumps(roles)}\n"
            f"Profile: rows {profile['rows']}, bytes {profile['bytes']}\nColumns: {json.dumps(profile['columns'], ensure_ascii=False)[:6000]}\n"
            + (f"Your previous proposal was rejected: {problems}. Fix exactly these.\n" if problems else ""))
    return llm.chat(f"reduction {source_id}", system, user, max_tokens=900)


def verify(proposal: dict, kind: str, profile: dict, path: Path) -> list[str]:
    import duckdb  # noqa: PLC0415

    have = {c["name"] for c in profile["columns"]}
    keep = proposal.get("keep") or []; drop = [d.get("column") for d in proposal.get("drop") or []]
    bad = [f"unknown column in keep: {c}" for c in keep if c not in have]
    bad += [f"unknown column in drop: {c}" for c in drop if c not in have]
    bad += [f"column neither kept nor dropped: {c}" for c in sorted(have - set(keep) - set(drop))]
    bad += [f"column both kept and dropped: {c}" for c in sorted(set(keep) & set(drop))]
    roles = proposal.get("roles") or {}
    for role in ROLES.get(kind, {}):
        col = roles.get(role)
        if role == "variable" and kind == "weather":
            if not any(c in keep for c in have - {roles.get("timestamp"), roles.get("station")}): bad.append("no weather variable kept")
            continue
        if not col: bad.append(f"required role {role} not mapped")
        elif col not in have: bad.append(f"role {role} mapped to unknown column {col}")
        elif col not in keep: bad.append(f"required role {role} ({col}) was dropped")
    con = duckdb.connect(); con.execute(f"CREATE VIEW t AS SELECT * FROM read_parquet('{path}')")
    for f in proposal.get("row_filters") or []:
        sql = f.get("sql", "")
        if not sql or any(w in sql.lower() for w in (";", "drop ", "delete ", "update ", "insert ", "copy ", "attach")):
            bad.append(f"filter refused: {sql[:80]}"); continue
        try:
            con.execute(f"SELECT count(*) FROM t WHERE {sql}")
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            bad.append(f"filter does not parse: {sql[:80]} ({str(exc)[:80]})")
    return bad

    import duckdb  # noqa: PLC0415

    t0 = time.time(); con = duckdb.connect()
    con.execute(f"CREATE VIEW t AS SELECT * FROM read_parquet('{path}')")
    before = con.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM t").fetchone()[0]
    keep = ", ".join(f'"{c}"' for c in proposal["keep"])
    filters, where = [], []
    for f in proposal.get("row_filters") or []:
        n = con.execute(f"SELECT count(*) FROM t WHERE NOT ({f['sql']}) OR ({f['sql']}) IS NULL").fetchone()[0]
        filters.append({"sql": f["sql"], "reason": f.get("reason", ""), "rows_removed_alone": int(n)})
        where.append(f"({f['sql']})")
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    con.execute(f"COPY (SELECT {keep} FROM t WHERE {' AND '.join(where) if where else 'TRUE'}) TO '{out}' (FORMAT PARQUET)")
    after = con.execute(f"SELECT count(*) FROM read_parquet('{out}')").fetchone()[0]
    return {"path": str(out), "rows_before": int(before), "rows_after": int(after), "columns_before": len(proposal["keep"]) + len(proposal.get("drop") or []),
            "columns_after": len(proposal["keep"]), "bytes_before": path.stat().st_size, "bytes_after": out.stat().st_size,
            "filters": filters, "dropped": proposal.get("drop") or [], "roles": proposal.get("roles"), "reasoning": proposal.get("reasoning", ""),
            "seconds": round(time.time() - t0, 1)}

"""The agentic retrieval loop, end to end: search, assess, probe (v1) then fetch and dilute (new).

    OPENAI_API_KEY=... python -m discover.run_v2 --out discover/results_v2 --months 1 --rows-per-month 400000

Stages 1-3 are run.py unchanged: registries searched with agent-proposed queries, deterministic
gates, live probes, agent relevance and schema maps verified by code. Stage 4 (acquire.py) has
the agent write a retrieval plan per surviving source and code execute it. Stage 5 (reduce.py)
has the agent decide, per fetched table, which columns and rows the training set keeps, and code
verify and apply it. REPORT.md lists every decision with its reason and its measured effect.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime as dt
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from . import acquire, llm, reduce
from .spec import DataSpec

NEED = (
    "Training records for a route-planning TSLM: one record = one service group (train type -> final destination) at one "
    "station on one travel date. Inputs are aggregates over the 7 to 120 days before the travel date: mean departure delay "
    "of the service and of the station, cancellation rate, stop counts (throughput), and shares of delay minutes by IRIS "
    "cause family; target = mean departure delay of that service at that station over the following week. Annotations: "
    "public and school holidays per federal state, station category / federal state / weight, dated works notices, "
    "weather as context. From an events source we need stop-level rows with: event time, station name (and id), train "
    "type, train number or line, final destination, delay minutes, arrival/departure cancellation flags, the ride id and "
    "stop sequence number. Buses are out of scope. Planned vs changed timestamps are the label's ingredients, not inputs."
)


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="discover/results_v2", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--months", type=int, default=1)
    ap.add_argument("--rows-per-month", type=int, default=400_000)
    ap.add_argument("--weather-days", type=int, default=7)
    ap.add_argument("--weather-stations", type=int, default=3)
    ap.add_argument("--skip-search", action="store_true", help="reuse <out>/assessment.json from an earlier run")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    out: Path = args.out; out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    spec = DataSpec()
    budget = {"max_months": args.months, "max_rows_per_month": args.rows_per_month, "max_weather_days": args.weather_days,
              "max_weather_stations": args.weather_stations}

    if not args.skip_search or not (out / "assessment.json").exists():
        from . import run as v1  # noqa: PLC0415
        sys.argv = ["discover.run", "--out", str(out)]
        v1.main()
    entries = json.loads((out / "assessment.json").read_text())["entries"]
    live = [e for e in entries if e["accepted"] and e.get("probe", {}).get("probed") and acquire.PLAN_SCHEMAS.get(e["id"])]
    print(f"\nacquire: {len(live)} sources have a live probe and an executor: {[e['id'] for e in live]}")

    acquisition = []
    data_dir = out / "data"
    for e in live:
        rec = {"id": e["id"], "kind": e.get("kind")}
        plan = acquire.plan_for(e, NEED, spec.window, budget)
        if not plan:
            rec["status"] = "no plan (agent unavailable or failed)"; acquisition.append(rec); print(f"  {e['id']}: {rec['status']}"); continue
        problems = acquire.validate_plan(e, plan, spec.window, budget)
        rec["first_plan"], rec["first_plan_problems"] = plan, problems
        if problems:
            plan = acquire.plan_for(e, NEED, spec.window, budget, problems) or {}
            problems = acquire.validate_plan(e, plan, spec.window, budget) if plan else ["no second plan"]
            rec["second_plan"], rec["second_plan_problems"] = plan, problems
        if problems:
            rec["status"] = f"skipped: plan rejected twice ({'; '.join(problems)[:200]})"; acquisition.append(rec); print(f"  {e['id']}: {rec['status']}"); continue
        try:
            rec["manifest"] = acquire.execute(e, plan, data_dir / e["id"].replace(":", "_").replace("/", "_"))
            rec["status"] = "fetched"
            m = rec["manifest"]; print(f"  {e['id']}: fetched {m['rows']} rows x {m['columns']} cols, {m['bytes']/1e6:.1f} MB in {m['seconds']}s")
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            rec["status"] = f"fetch failed: {str(exc)[:200]}"; print(f"  {e['id']}: {rec['status']}")
        acquisition.append(rec)
    (out / "acquisition.json").write_text(json.dumps(acquisition, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, default=str))

    reduction = []
    for rec in acquisition:
        if rec.get("status") != "fetched": continue
        path = Path(rec["manifest"]["path"]); kind = rec["kind"] if rec["kind"] in reduce.ROLES else "reference"
        prof = reduce.profile_table(path)
        prop = reduce.propose(rec["id"], kind, NEED, prof)
        r = {"id": rec["id"], "kind": kind, "profile": prof}
        if not prop:
            r["status"] = "no proposal"; reduction.append(r); continue
        problems = reduce.verify(prop, kind, prof, path)
        r["first_proposal"], r["first_problems"] = prop, problems
        if problems:
            prop = reduce.propose(rec["id"], kind, NEED, prof, problems) or {}
            problems = reduce.verify(prop, kind, prof, path) if prop else ["no second proposal"]
            r["second_proposal"], r["second_problems"] = prop, problems
        if problems:
            r["status"] = f"kept whole: proposal rejected twice ({'; '.join(problems)[:200]})"; reduction.append(r)
            print(f"  {rec['id']}: {r['status']}"); continue
        r["applied"] = reduce.apply(path, prop, out / "reduced" / path.name)
        r["status"] = "reduced"
        a = r["applied"]
        print(f"  {rec['id']}: {a['rows_before']}->{a['rows_after']} rows, {a['columns_before']}->{a['columns_after']} cols, "
              f"{a['bytes_before']/1e6:.1f}->{a['bytes_after']/1e6:.1f} MB; dropped {[d['column'] for d in a['dropped']]}")
        reduction.append(r)
    (out / "reduction.json").write_text(json.dumps(reduction, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, default=str))
    (out / "agent_log.json").write_text(json.dumps(llm.LOG, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))

    lines = ["# Agentic retrieval, run of record (v2)", "",
             f"Generated {dt.datetime.now(dt.UTC):%Y-%m-%d %H:%M} UTC. Agent: {llm.MODEL if llm.available() else 'none'}, {len(llm.LOG)} calls in total "
             f"(search, assessment, schema maps, retrieval plans, reductions). Budget: {json.dumps(budget)}.", "",
             "## Stage 4: what the agent chose to fetch, and what code did with it", "",
             "| source | plan (agent) | verifier | fetched |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
    for rec in acquisition:
        plan = rec.get("second_plan") or rec.get("first_plan") or {}
        ver = "accepted first plan" if not rec.get("first_plan_problems") else ("accepted after re-prompt: " + "; ".join(rec["first_plan_problems"])[:120] if rec.get("status") == "fetched" else "rejected twice")
        m = rec.get("manifest"); got = f"{m['rows']} rows x {m['columns']} cols, {m['bytes']/1e6:.1f} MB, {m['seconds']}s" if m else rec.get("status", "")
        lines.append(f"| `{rec['id']}` | {json.dumps({k: v for k, v in plan.items() if k != 'reasoning'}, ensure_ascii=False)[:220]} — {plan.get('reasoning', '')[:160]} | {ver} | {got} |")
    lines += ["", "## Stage 5: how the agent diluted each table, and the measured effect", ""]
    for r in reduction:
        lines.append(f"### `{r['id']}`"); lines.append("")
        a = r.get("applied")
        if not a:
            lines.append(f"{r.get('status')}"); lines.append(""); continue
        lines.append(f"{a['rows_before']:,} -> {a['rows_after']:,} rows, {a['columns_before']} -> {a['columns_after']} columns, "
                     f"{a['bytes_before']/1e6:.1f} -> {a['bytes_after']/1e6:.1f} MB. Roles: {json.dumps(a['roles'], ensure_ascii=False)}")
        lines.append(""); lines.append(f"Agent's reasoning: {a['reasoning'][:500]}"); lines.append("")
        if a["dropped"]:
            lines += ["| dropped column | agent's reason |", "|---|---|"] + [f"| `{d['column']}` | {d.get('reason', '')[:160]} |" for d in a["dropped"]] + [""]
        if a["filters"]:
            lines += ["| row filter | agent's reason | rows it removes alone |", "|---|---|---:|"] + [f"| `{f['sql'][:90]}` | {f['reason'][:140]} | {f['rows_removed_alone']:,} |" for f in a["filters"]] + [""]
        if r.get("first_problems"):
            lines.append(f"Verifier objected to the first proposal: {'; '.join(r['first_problems'])[:300]}"); lines.append("")
    (out / "REPORT.md").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    print(f"\nwrote {out}/acquisition.json, reduction.json, REPORT.md, agent_log.json ({len(llm.LOG)} agent calls)")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

**v2 agentic retrieval: finished, end to end, committed locally on `feat/agentic-retrieval-v2` (2ba9933), nothing pushed.** The agent now does two things the v1 loop never did, and code applies its decisions instead of overruling them.

**Stage 4, the agent fetches.** For every source that passed the gates and the live probe, the agent wrote a retrieval plan under a budget; code checked each plan against the probe and executed it:

| source | agent's plan | fetched |
|---|---|---|
| DB archive (piebro) | November 2025, all 17 columns, no station filter, 400k-row cap | 400,000 rows in 3 s |
| OpenHolidays | Bavaria, public and school holidays | 20 rows |
| DB stations | id, category, federal state | 5,388 rows |
| Bright Sky weather | 11 variables, 3 hub stations, one week | 435 rows |

Two plans were rejected on the first try and fixed on the re-prompt: for the station hub the agent asked for fields the source does not have, for weather it asked for delay variables and a span past the budget.

**Stage 5, the agent dilutes.** Code profiled each fetched table (types, null rates, cardinality, correlation with the delay target); the agent decided what the training set keeps, with a reason per column and per filter; code verified the required roles survive and applied it:

- Events: 17 to 10 columns, 400,000 to 386,698 rows. Dropped the planned and changed timestamps ("the label's ingredients, not inputs"), the ids, the EVA. Filtered out buses, 13,302 rows. Size 17.2 to 6.5 MB.
- Holidays: dropped the free-text name and a duplicate of `kind`.

content.text:
Compared directly, both branches in front of me. Here is the exact difference, and an honest answer on relevance.

**What the branch version does (v1).** Search with agent-proposed queries, deterministic gates, live probes, then the agent judges relevance, fills the rubric and proposes a schema map, and code verifies each. Its output is decisions: an assessment file and a rejection table. It fetches no bytes. The data the models trained on was fetched and shaped by hand-written connector code; the agent only confirmed the choice of sources.

**What v2 adds.** Same first three stages, then two stages where the agent's decisions are executed:

| | v1 on the branch | v2 |
|---|---|---|
| chooses which sources | agent, verified by code | same |
| chooses what to fetch (months, columns, filters, fields, variables, stations) | hand-written | agent plans, code validates against the probe and executes |
| chooses what the training set keeps (columns, row filters) | hand-designed features | agent decides per table with a reason each, code verifies roles and applies |
| output | decision files | decision files plus fetched tables plus reduced tables plus a measured report |
| agent calls in the run of record | 34 | 79 |

**Generality: better in the decision layer, not in transport.** The reduction stage is generic: any parquet table, any need description, role sets per data kind. The retrieval plan prompt is generic. What is not generic is the fetch itself: each API shape needs an executor, and there are four. A new source with a new API needs a new executor before the agent can plan for it. That is the honest limit.

**Relevance of what it retrieved: not better than v1, and in three places worse.** The sources are identical because the same gates admit the same 18 of 354 candidates; v2 did not find anything v1 had not. Inside those sources the agent's choices were:

- Right on the primary table. It dropped the planned and changed timestamps as label ingredients, dropped ids, filtered buses. That matches what the hand-built pipeline does, and it got there from the need description alone.
- Right on holidays. Dropped free text and a duplicate column.
- Wrong three times, all recorded in the report: it dropped the stop sequence number the pipeline needs to rebuild runs, dropped station category which we use as an annotation, and reduced weather to the text field `condition`, throwing away temperature and precipitation.
- Narrow by budget: one month, Bavaria only, three weather stations. Fine for the run of record, not a training corpus.

So v2 made the agent real in the sense you asked for: its decisions now determine what is fetched and what the training data looks like, and every one is logged with its reason and its measured effect. It did not make the data more relevant than the hand-built pipeline, and its outputs are not wired into the connector, so the models trained today never saw them. Wiring them in and letting a human overrule the three bad calls in the report is the next step, after the deadline.

no, i wanna know how to improve and automate the data retrieval using agentic ai for tsml typa data. how to make it better than the manual solution of hand-picking datasets. what is the solution to use the best type of possible tsml train dataset which doesnt overfit or underfit

The short version: today's loop, v1 and v2 alike, is a librarian. It checks licences, coverage and columns, and asks the agent for opinions. A hand-picker beats it because the human is silently using the one signal the loop never sees: whether the model gets better. The way to beat hand-picking is to give the agent that signal and let it search over datasets the way it would search over hyperparameters.

**The architecture that actually beats manual picking**

1. **Make the dataset a function of a small spec.** We already have most of this: profile (resolution and context length), anchor stride (corpus size), channel list, source list, horizon, entity selection. Every knob is a build argument to the connector.
2. **Give the agent a cheap, honest score.** Gradient boosting on the same per-series summaries, on the same held-out cells, runs in two minutes on a laptop and today tracked the TSLM within 0.05 minutes on every cell. That is the proxy. The full TSLM run is reserved for the top two or three variants.
3. **Close the loop.** The agent proposes a variant with a stated hypothesis ("adding precipitation should help winter weeks"; "halving anchor stride should reduce variance"), code builds it, scores it, and hands back the numbers with the seed noise floor. The agent keeps or discards and proposes the next. Stop when no proposal beats the noise floor, which today is 0.02 minutes on unseen trains.

That turns "the agent chose which columns" from an opinion, which is what v2 does and gets wrong three times, into a measured ablation. It is the difference between an agent that reasons about data and an agent that experiments on it.

**What the agent should search over, in order of what we measured today**

- **Corpus size before anything else.** 5,200 training records was the binding constraint: 2k steps was the optimum and 12k collapsed coverage to 0.2. Anchor stride is the lever: weekly instead of 35-day anchors gives about five times the records at zero new sources.
- Context length and resolution. Quarter beat week and season; multiscale added nothing. Measured, done.
- Channels. Drop or add one, rescore. This is where the agent's column reasoning becomes a hypothesis generator rather than a decision maker.
- Extra sources. Weather, works notices, infrastructure. Admit only if the proxy gain beats the noise floor.

**The overfit and underfit rule, made mechanical**

- **Steps come from the record count, never from another project.** Two to four passes over the training set. Our sweet spot was three; nineteen destroyed it. Jonas's 12k steps are a third of a pass over his 300k examples, which is why the same number meant opposite things.
- **Pick the checkpoint, don't pick the step count.** The script already saves every 500 steps. Score each saved checkpoint on validation and keep the one with the best CRPS, with a hard guard that the 80% range must cover at least 70% of outcomes. Today that guard alone would have rejected every 12k model.
- **Hold out by time and by entity, and always score persistence and gradient boosting on the same rows.** A model that does not beat the entity's own context mean has learned nothing, whatever its loss says.

**Guards that stay deterministic, no agent involved**

Leakage (no label ingredient in any input column, purge at the split boundary), the station-basis step on 2025-11-02, constant series, duplicated anchors whose contexts overlap almost entirely. The validator has most of these already; the agent must not be able to switch them off.

**Cost to build it from what exists.** The connector is already parameterised, the proxy scorer is `baselines_local.py`, the validator exists. The missing piece is the loop itself: propose, build, score, log, about 200 lines, plus two connector knobs for anchor stride and channel list. Half a day. Then the run of record stops being "the agent agreed with our sources" and becomes "the agent found the dataset variant that scored best, and here is every variant it tried".

No guarantee, and the paper does not offer one either. What it offers, together with the deck, is three concrete things we did not do, plus the rules that make overfitting detectable instead of hoped away.

**What the paper actually does** ([arXiv 2510.02410](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.02410)): two stages. First a warm-up on synthetic question answering and M4 captions so the encoder and projector learn to read series at all. Then the task datasets, HAR-CoT, Sleep-CoT and ECG-QA-CoT, where every sample carries a chain-of-thought rationale written by GPT-4o from the plot and the ground-truth answer, and for ECG validated by cardiologists. Splits 80/10/10. Text-only baselines score zero on HAR because the series are long. Its own stated limitation: "framing tasks as natural language generation does not ensure that the model prioritizes the correct label after presenting its rationale, underscoring the need for loss functions that explicitly enforce correct answers", and "curated datasets likely lead to better rationales". It reports no dataset-size ablation, so it says nothing about our overfitting problem.

**Three things to take from it, in order of how much they change our situation**

1. **The data profile the deck asks for is series plus reasoning text per sample.** Slide 13, verbatim: "A dataset with time-series and text reasoning over it / or describing it. In some cases you might consider generating text annotations with LLMs (as in OpenTSLM paper)." Our records carry a template sentence with numbers filled in. Jonas's carry a template too. Neither is reasoning. This is where an agentic pipeline earns its place beyond sourcing: an LLM writes a per-record rationale from the series and the known outcome, and a validator refuses any rationale whose numbers are not in the record or whose conclusion contradicts the label. That is the paper's cardiologist check, automated, and it is the "validation" verb from the bonus slide.
2. **Give the encoder signal that text cannot hold.** Slide 8's whole thesis is "no context wall". Our quarter profile is 240 points per series, which fits in a prompt, which is exactly why Jonas found text beats the encoder on short series and why our model ties gradient boosting. Hourly over 120 days is 2,880 points per series, under the 4,096 cap, and that is the regime the paper wins in. The closed loop should search resolution and span with the explicit objective "beat the text baseline", not just "beat persistence".
3. **Select checkpoints by validation, never by step count.** The paper picks its baselines "by validation loss". We picked 12k because Jonas did. Save every 500 steps, score each on validation, keep the best, and refuse any whose 80% range covers less than 70% of outcomes.

**What guards against the same problems.** Not a guarantee, but a set of tests that make failure visible before it ships: held-out cells by time and by entity as the deck demands, three seeds so noise has a number, persistence and gradient boosting scored on the same rows, the calibration guard, the leakage checks in the validator. Today those tests caught the 12k collapse within twenty minutes of the first eval. That is the most anyone can honestly promise.

**Where the agent fits in that picture.** Not choosing columns by opinion, which is where v2 was wrong three times. Proposing dataset variants along those three axes, reading the measured result, and writing and validating the rationales. That is an agent doing science on the data instead of cataloguing it.

"""v3: a closed loop over dataset variants, scored by a cheap proxy on held-out validation.

The agent proposes a variant of the training set (which series channels to keep) with a stated
hypothesis; code builds the variant's feature table from the registry, fits gradient boosting
(the proxy that tracked the TSLM within 0.05 min on every cell today) on the training split and
scores CRPS on validation; the agent reads the result against the noise floor and proposes the
next. Stops when a proposal cannot beat the incumbent by more than the noise floor, or after
--rounds. Only validation is used for selection; the test cells are scored once, for the winner.

    python -m discover.search_loop --registry <dir> --profile quarter --rounds 5 --out discover/results_v3
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

from . import llm

NOISE_FLOOR = 0.02  # CRPS spread between three seeds of the same recipe on the same rows (13 Sep 2026)
LEAKY = {"attributed_share", "artifact_bundle_sha", "split", "split_cell", "recency_weight"}
LEVELS = np.array([0.05, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.35, 0.4, 0.45, 0.5, 0.55, 0.6, 0.65, 0.7, 0.75, 0.8, 0.85, 0.9, 0.95])


def crps(y: np.ndarray, q: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """Pinball loss averaged over the 19 quantile levels: the same proper score the runs report."""
    d = y[:, None] - q
    return float(np.mean(np.maximum(LEVELS * d, (LEVELS - 1) * d)) * 2)


def load(registry: str, profile: str, bridge):
    from timenet.client import TimeNet  # noqa: PLC0415

    ds = TimeNet(registry).load(f"error404/db-route-{profile}")
    keys = sorted({k for r in ds.records for k, v in bridge.annotation_map(r).items()
                   if isinstance(v, (int, float)) and not isinstance(v, bool) and k not in LEAKY})
    rows = []
    for r in ds.records:
        ann = bridge.annotation_map(r)
        y = next((float(t.target) for t in ds.tasks_for(r) if type(t).__name__ == "ScalarPredictionTask"), None)
        if y is None:
            continue
        series = {t.signal: np.asarray(t.to_numpy(), dtype=float) for t in r.time_series}
        rows.append({"id": str(r.record_id), "split": ann.get("split"), "cell": ann.get("split_cell", ann.get("split")), "y": y,
                     "scalars": [float(ann[k]) if isinstance(ann.get(k), (int, float)) else np.nan for k in keys], "series": series})
    signals = sorted({s for row in rows for s in row["series"]})
    return rows, keys, signals


def features(rows: list[dict], keep: list[str]) -> np.ndarray:
    out = []
    for row in rows:
        f = list(row["scalars"])
        for s in keep:
            v = row["series"].get(s)
            f += [np.nanmean(v), np.nanstd(v), float(v[-1]), np.nanmax(v)] if v is not None and v.size else [np.nan] * 4
        out.append(f)
    return np.array(out, dtype=float)


def score(rows: list[dict], keep: list[str], cells: tuple[str, ...] = ("val",)) -> dict:
    from sklearn.ensemble import HistGradientBoostingRegressor as HGB  # noqa: PLC0415

    tr = [r for r in rows if r["split"] == "train"]
    Xt, yt = features(tr, keep), np.array([r["y"] for r in tr])
    ok = np.array([np.isfinite(Xt[:, j]).any() and np.nanstd(Xt[:, j]) > 0 for j in range(Xt.shape[1])])
    Xt = Xt[:, ok]
    models = {lv: HGB(loss="quantile", quantile=lv, max_iter=200, max_depth=6, learning_rate=0.05, random_state=0).fit(Xt, yt) for lv in LEVELS}
    out = {}
    for cell in cells:
        rs = [r for r in rows if r["cell"] == cell]
        X, y = features(rs, keep)[:, ok], np.array([r["y"] for r in rs])
        Q = np.sort(np.stack([models[lv].predict(X) for lv in LEVELS], axis=1), axis=1)
        out[cell] = {"n": len(rs), "crps": round(crps(y, Q), 4), "median_error": round(float(np.abs(Q[:, 9] - y).mean()), 4),
                     "coverage_10_90": round(float(((y >= Q[:, 1]) & (y <= Q[:, 17])).mean()), 3)}
    return out


def propose(signals: list[str], history: list[dict], need: str) -> dict | None:
    system = ("You are searching for the best training-set variant for a train-delay forecasting model. A variant is the "
              "list of series channels to KEEP (all others are dropped). Reply with one JSON object: "
              '{"keep": [channels], "hypothesis": "one sentence on why this should beat the incumbent", "stop": false}. '
              "Set stop=true with an explanation in 'hypothesis' if you believe no variant can beat the incumbent by more "
              "than the noise floor. Propose exactly one variant per round; do not repeat a tried variant.")
    user = (f"Need: {need}\nChannels available: {signals}\nNoise floor (CRPS): {NOISE_FLOOR}\n"
            f"Rounds so far (lower CRPS is better; the first row is the incumbent with every channel):\n"
            + "\n".join(json.dumps({k: h[k] for k in ("round", "keep", "hypothesis", "val")}, ensure_ascii=False) for h in history))
    return llm.chat("dataset variant", system, user, max_tokens=500)


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--registry", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--profile", default="quarter")
    ap.add_argument("--rounds", type=int, default=5)
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="discover/results_v3", type=Path)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
    import bridge  # noqa: PLC0415

    args.out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    t0 = time.time()
    rows, keys, signals = load(args.registry, args.profile, bridge)
    print(f"loaded {len(rows)} scalar rows, {len(keys)} scalar annotations, {len(signals)} channels in {time.time() - t0:.0f}s", flush=True)
    need = ("Forecast next week's mean departure delay of a service group at a station from 60 days of six-hourly history "
            "(the quarter profile) plus calendar and station annotations; scored by CRPS on held-out validation.")
    history = []
    base = score(rows, signals)
    history.append({"round": 0, "keep": signals, "hypothesis": "incumbent: every channel", "val": base["val"], "accepted": True})
    best = history[0]
    print(f"round 0 incumbent: val CRPS {base['val']['crps']} (all {len(signals)} channels)", flush=True)
    for rnd in range(1, args.rounds + 1):
        prop = propose(signals, history, need) if llm.available() else None
        if not prop:
            print("agent unavailable or failed; stopping", flush=True); break
        if prop.get("stop"):
            history.append({"round": rnd, "keep": None, "hypothesis": prop.get("hypothesis", ""), "val": None, "accepted": False, "stop": True})
            print(f"round {rnd}: agent stops: {prop.get('hypothesis', '')[:160]}", flush=True); break
        keep = [s for s in prop.get("keep") or [] if s in signals]
        if not keep or any(keep == h["keep"] for h in history):
            history.append({"round": rnd, "keep": keep, "hypothesis": prop.get("hypothesis", ""), "val": None, "accepted": False,
                            "note": "empty or repeated variant, not scored"}); continue
        res = score(rows, keep)
        gain = best["val"]["crps"] - res["val"]["crps"]
        accepted = gain > NOISE_FLOOR
        h = {"round": rnd, "keep": keep, "hypothesis": prop.get("hypothesis", ""), "val": res["val"], "gain_vs_incumbent": round(gain, 4), "accepted": accepted}
        history.append(h)
        print(f"round {rnd}: keep {len(keep)}/{len(signals)} -> val CRPS {res['val']['crps']} (gain {gain:+.4f}, {'ACCEPTED' if accepted else 'rejected'}) | {h['hypothesis'][:120]}", flush=True)
        if accepted:
            best = h
    final = score(rows, best["keep"], ("val", "test_seen_entity", "test", "test_seen_time"))
    result = {"profile": args.profile, "registry": args.registry, "noise_floor": NOISE_FLOOR, "channels": signals, "history": history,
              "winner": {"keep": best["keep"], "dropped": [s for s in signals if s not in best["keep"]], "scores": final},
              "agent": {"model": llm.MODEL if llm.available() else None, "calls": len(llm.LOG)}}
    (args.out / "search.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
    (args.out / "agent_log_search.json").write_text(json.dumps(llm.LOG, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
    lines = ["# Dataset variant search (v3)", "", f"Profile {args.profile}, proxy = gradient boosting on per-channel summaries + annotations, "
             f"selection on validation CRPS only, noise floor {NOISE_FLOOR}. Agent: {result['agent']['model']}, {result['agent']['calls']} calls.", "",
             "| round | channels kept | hypothesis (agent) | val CRPS | gain | verdict |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for h in history:
        v = h.get("val") or {}
        lines.append(f"| {h['round']} | {len(h['keep']) if h.get('keep') else '-'} | {h['hypothesis'][:140]} | {v.get('crps', '')} | {h.get('gain_vs_incumbent', '')} | "
                     f"{'stop' if h.get('stop') else 'accepted' if h.get('accepted') else h.get('note', 'rejected')} |")
    lines += ["", f"Winner keeps {len(best['keep'])} of {len(signals)} channels; dropped: {result['winner']['dropped']}", "",
              "| cell | n | median error | CRPS | coverage 10-90 |", "|---|---:|---|---|---|"]
    for c, s in final.items():
        lines.append(f"| {c} | {s['n']} | {s['median_error']:.3f} | {s['crps']:.3f} | {s['coverage_10_90']:.2f} |")
    (args.out / "SEARCH.md").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    print(f"wrote {args.out}/search.json, SEARCH.md; winner drops {result['winner']['dropped']}", flush=True)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

**v3 variant search finished and is committed locally (4db3db5).** Five rounds, five agent proposals, each scored on validation, none accepted. The incumbent with all ten channels stands at val CRPS 1.388. The interesting round is the last one: a five-channel variant tied the incumbent within 0.0006, which says half the channels carry the signal and the other half cost nothing but add nothing. The loop's rule was "beat the incumbent by more than the noise floor", so it kept all ten. A parsimony rule would take the five. Round 2 also shows the loop working as intended: a plausible-sounding proposal lost 0.14 and was rejected on the number, not on the story.

what exactly is the v3 agentic data retrieval ? what happeend there

v3 is the "agent does experiments on the data, not opinions about it" version. Two pieces, both committed locally on `feat/agentic-retrieval-v3` (4db3db5), nothing pushed.

**Piece 1: a closed-loop search over dataset variants, scored by a number.** In v2 the agent said which columns to keep and code applied it, so the agent's judgment was the final word, and it was wrong three times. In v3 the agent's judgment is a hypothesis and a measurement is the final word:

1. Code loads the all-Germany quarter registry: 10,204 records, 10 series channels, 11 scalar annotations.
2. The incumbent is "keep all 10 channels". Code scores it with the proxy: gradient boosting on per-channel summaries plus annotations, fitted on train, scored by CRPS on validation. Result 1.388.
3. Each round the agent sees every previous round's variant, hypothesis and score, and proposes one new set of channels to keep with one sentence of reasoning.
4. Code builds that variant's feature table, fits, scores on validation, and accepts only if it beats the incumbent by more than the noise floor of 0.02, the spread we measured between three seeds of the same recipe this morning.
5. Only the final winner is scored on the test cells.

What happened in the run of record, five rounds:

| round | channels kept | val CRPS | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 incumbent | 10 | 1.388 | stands |
| 1 | 4 | 1.392 | rejected |
| 2 | 4 | 1.526 | rejected, lost 0.14 |
| 3 | 4 | 1.403 | rejected |
| 4 | 4 | 1.405 | rejected |
| 5 | 5 | 1.387 | rejected, tie |

Every proposal came with a plausible story. Round 2's story was as convincing as the others and lost 0.14. Round 5 found five channels that tie all ten, which means half the channels carry nothing, but the rule was "beat, not tie", so all ten stay. That is the point of the design: the agent's stories no longer decide anything on their own.

**Piece 2: the trainer picks its checkpoint by validation, not by step count.** The 12k collapse this morning happened because the step count was copied from a project with sixty times the data. The v3 trainer saves every 250 steps, scores 300 validation rows at each save, and evaluates the checkpoint with the best validation CRPS, with the whole curve written to the metrics. It also takes the channel set the search chose. That trainer is running now as `v3-q-valsel`, quarter, 3k steps, every held-out row scored, lands about 11:50.

**What v3 does not do yet, and should.** No per-record reasoning text, which is the data profile the deck asks for. No search over resolution and span, the axis where the paper says the encoder beats text. No new sources. Those are the next levers, in that order, and they need the same loop: propose, build, score, keep or discard.

content.text:
Page is up: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/2d2df046-1f39-4d36-ba32-b6f028958597

What it shows, per fetched source:

- **DB timetable archive**: 400,000 rows × 17 columns fetched in 3 s. The agent's cut: 386,698 rows × 10 columns, 17.2 to 6.5 MB. Each of the 17 columns with type, null rate, distinct count, sample values, correlation with the delay, and the agent's verdict with its reason. Struck through: the planned and changed timestamps ("the label's ingredients, not inputs"), two ids, the EVA, the stop sequence. The one row filter, buses out, removed 13,302 rows. First five rows of the reduced table.
- **OpenHolidays**: 20 rows × 7 columns, cut to 4. Dropped the free-text name, a duplicate of `kind`, a boolean. The verifier's objection to its first proposal is shown too.
- **DB station hub**: 5,388 rows, the agent asked for three fields and then dropped `category`.
- **Bright Sky weather**: 435 rows × 13 columns cut to 3, keeping only `condition`. The page shows exactly which variables it threw away.

Below that, the v3 variant search table, round by round with the agent's hypothesis, validation CRPS, gain and verdict, and then eight of the 40 sources the agent rejected before any fetch with its stated reason each, plus the gate rejections grouped by the gate that failed.

Monitoring is now once every 5 minutes, and only the v3 job is still running. Eval lines, the validation curve, errors and state changes still come through immediately.

cd /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-gaurav-Downloads-zurich-lates-temporal-ai-error404-ai/6f11fbbe-b41b-4ac6-96cf-af296c485bf7/scratchpad && cat > connector-deck.html <<'EOF' The TimeNet Connector

Temporal AI Challenge · step 02 CONNECT · slide text

The TimeNet Connector

What happens between "the data is retrieved" and "the model trains". Each section below is written as one slide: a headline, a one-liner, the bullets, and a sentence to say out loud. Numbers are from the all-Germany build of 13 September 2026.

One connector body, four TimeNet datasets

Slide 1 · the claim

The connector turns ten months of Deutsche Bahn timetable events into a validated, reproducible TimeNet dataset: one record per train service at one station on one travel date, with its history as time series, its context as annotations, and four questions as tasks.

  • Dataset ids: error404/db-route-week, -quarter, -season, -multiscale. Same entities, anchors, labels and splits in all four; only the history before each anchor differs.
  • Scale: all of Germany, November 2025 to August 2026, 2,539 stations, 722 service groups, about 10,200 to 11,200 records per profile.
  • Contract: TimeNet BaseConnector with two methods, download() for every network read and convert() for a pure, offline transformation. Built with timenet-build build error404/db-route-quarter, loaded with TimeNet(root).load(id).

Say: TimeNet is the boundary of our lane. Everything the model ever sees passes through this connector, and nothing model-specific is inside it: no tokens, no prompts, no normalisation. That is what makes it reusable.

Where it sits

Slide 2 · the pipeline in one picture

Say: The agentic retrieval decides which sources; the connector decides what a training example is. Two different jobs, one boundary between them.

download(): build the fact cache once, never re-read the archive

Slide 3 · the network half

All network work happens here and lands in a local cache that every profile shares.

  • Hourly fact tables per station, per service group, and per (service, station) pair. They store sums and counts, never means: re-bucketing a mean of means across hours with different train counts is biased; every coarser bucket is sum(sum_delay) / sum(n_obs).
  • Cause codes and disruption notices come from the archived raw IRIS XML, which the processed files drop. Two extractors: per-stop delay causes (types d, f, q, a numeric code mapped to six families) and dated planned-disruption notices (type h, with from/to validity, priority, publication time). Day-sharded and resumable: a shard that exists is never refetched.
  • External context: OpenHolidays (public and school holidays per federal state) and the DB station hub (EVA, federal state, category, weight).
  • Basis pinned: the archive expands from ~100 to all stations on 2 November 2025. Aggregates use a fixed station universe so a 60- or 120-day series never carries a manufactured regime change, and the validator asserts it.

Say: The archive tells you what happened; the raw XML tells you why. Nobody else in the archive's user base parses the XML for cause codes. That is the "why" tab in the app.

convert(): from facts to records

Slide 4 · the offline half

  • Entity = one service group (train type → final destination) at one station. Buses excluded. Service groups keyed on destination because line_number is empty for every long-distance train.
  • Anchor = a travel date at 00:00 local; five per entity, 35 days apart, staggered so the union spans the window; only anchors with a full 120 days of history before them.
  • Label = the mean departure delay of that service at that station over the seven days after the anchor, computed once and shared by all four profiles, so no profile can have a different target.
  • Resample = one SQL template over the fact cache for any (bucket, span): 1 h × 7 d, 6 h × 60 d, 1 d × 120 d, or all three. Missing buckets are imputed and counted; a record whose context is mostly empty is refused.
  • Bundle sha = a content hash over entities, anchors, labels and splits, stamped on every record. Identical across profiles by construction; the validator checks it.

Say: Four datasets are not four pipelines. They are one parameterised aggregation over one cache, which is why the bake-off between them is a controlled experiment and not four hand-made things.

What one record contains

Slide 5 · signals, metadata, annotations, tasks

TimeNet partWhat we put there
Signals (time series)Quarter profile, ten series on a six-hourly axis over 60 days: service delay, station delay, this service at this station, service throughput, station throughput, and shares of delay minutes by cause family (works, knock-on, technical, weather) plus the attributed share. Archival raw values in minutes and counts; no normalisation inside the dataset.
Metadata (span-less annotations)Station, service group, train type, anchor date, split and split cell, imputed fraction per grain, federal state, station category and weight, public holidays in the horizon, school-holiday share, days to and since a school holiday, and one caption per series naming the entity and window.
Annotations with a spanEvery planned-works notice that touched the station, as a TimeInterval with its real start and end dates, category and priority. Median notice lasts 22 days, so at the week profile a notice usually spans the whole context; the model reads coverage and position, not a flag. Only notices published before the anchor are attached.
Tasks1. Scalar prediction: next-week departure delay in minutes. 2. Classification: five or more minutes late, yes or no. 3. Classification: the dominant cause family, with a registered vocabulary. 4. Answer: one sentence a traveller can act on, chained off task 3.

Say: TimeNet has no metadata slot, so metadata is a span-less annotation; the dated works notice is the one thing most submissions leave unused, and it is exactly what a construction period is.

Four profiles, one experiment

Slide 6 · the bake-off

profilebucket × spanseriesencoder patchesrecordswhat it tests
week1 h × 7 d729411,119the operational week
quarter6 h × 60 d1060010,204the regime: works that started last month
season1 d × 120 d1030011,106seasonal level
multiscaleall three1983411,165does long history add on top of the week
  • Same anchors, labels, splits, seed and step budget in every run. The only variable is how much history precedes the anchor.
  • Result: quarter wins every held-out cell; week memorises; multiscale adds nothing at this budget. A pre-registered rule picked the winner on the unseen-trains cell.

Splits that cannot leak

Slide 7 · evaluation cells

  • Time cut at anchor-date quantiles 70 / 15 / 15, and 30% of entities held out entirely.
  • Four cells: val; test_seen_entity (known trains, unseen weeks: the deployment number); test (unseen trains and unseen weeks: the headline); test_seen_time (unseen trains, seen weeks: diagnostic only).
  • Purge of seven days at each time boundary; label ingredients (planned and changed timestamps of the horizon) never reach an input; notices filtered by publication time.
  • Quarter counts: train 5,166 · val 427 · seen-entity 1,134 · test 462 · seen-time 3,015.

Say: We publish the unseen-trains cell and the gap to the seen-trains cell as the memorisation estimate. A jury that sees us volunteer that number believes the honest one.

The validator: executable checks, fail closed

Slide 8 · why the dataset can be trusted

  • Source level, before any build: timestamps strictly monotonic within a run; no duplicate stop ids; planned-versus-actual sanity; no station-basis step across 2 November 2025.
  • Record level, at build: series count and length exactly as the profile says, all finite; imputed fraction under a per-grain budget and an overall cap; the answer line matches the task target; every number in a rationale exists in the record; a phase check cross-correlating station and service series, per record and as a consensus across records, which catches a one-hour timezone desynchronisation that is otherwise invisible.
  • Cross profile: identical bundle sha and identical split for every shared (entity, anchor) across the four datasets.
  • An error refuses the write; a warning is recorded in the report. 153 offline tests cover the pipeline and the connectors.

Reproducible for a stranger

Slide 9 · the reuse claim

  • Every record, series, annotation and task id is derived from source keys; every set is sorted before iteration. Two builds on two machines produced byte-identical datasets at Munich, six-region and all-Germany scale.
  • Dataset cards are JSON-schema validated; profile, bucket and span are tags on the card.
  • Credentials are optional and never change the output; a keyless run reproduces the dataset byte for byte.
  • Connector code is model-agnostic. The bridge to OpenTSLM (z-scoring, captions with mean and std, prompt assembly) lives outside the dataset, so swapping the LLM is a bridge argument, not a rebuild.

Who consumes it

Slide 10 · downstream

  • Training: a domain-agnostic bridge loads any TimeNet dataset into OpenTSLM samples. Tonight's runs trained Jonas's TripTSLM recipe on our four datasets without touching his code.
  • The app: the route model server reads the registry's annotations and the scored forecasts, answers /api/predict per leg and /api/causes per station, and the frontend shows the model's voice next to the prediction.
  • Refresh: the cause extraction is per day and skip-if-present, anchors and labels are derived, so extending the window is running the same connector with a later end date.

Limits, said plainly

Slide 11 · limitations

  • Imputed buckets are baked in because the model needs finite values; the imputed fraction is stored per record and the tension with "archival raw" is stated on the card.
  • The archive is published monthly, so the freshest anchor is the end of August; a daily batch would still be up to a month stale. The live signal for a running train is the other model.
  • A 5,200-record training corpus fits three to four passes at batch 8; twelve thousand steps overfit every profile, which the seed runs and the validation-selected checkpoints now guard against.

### Reading

- **The knee is between three and six passes.** 2k and 3k steps are indistinguishable (seed spread 0.02 CRPS); 4k is slightly worse; 6k loses calibration; 12k loses everything: median error +0.3 min, CRPS +0.5, and the 80% range covers a quarter of outcomes. ---
name: training-budget-lesson
description: Step counts are passes over the data; 12k steps overfit our 5k-record TimeF corpus, pick checkpoints by validation CRPS
metadata:
  type: project
---

On 13 Sep 2026 the db_route TSLM grid showed that 2k–3k steps (3–5 passes over ~5,200 training records at batch 8) is the knee; 6k loses calibration (coverage 0.58) and 12k (19 passes) collapses every profile (CRPS +0.5, coverage ~0.25). Jonas's 12k steps are a third of a pass over 300k examples, so his number does not transfer.

**Why:** the step budget was copied from a corpus sixty times larger; nothing in the recipe scaled it to record count.

**How to apply:** size steps as 2–4 passes over the training set, and prefer the v3 trainer's validation-selected checkpoint (`--save-every 250 --val-rows 300`). Guard: reject any checkpoint whose 10–90 coverage is below 0.7. Always run three seeds to know the noise floor (0.02 CRPS here). See [[bakeoff-outcome]] and [[smoke-before-provisioning]].

Also: zsh does not word-split an unquoted `$VAR` in `for t in $TAGS`; use literal lists or `${=TAGS}` in background scoring loops, and give parallel HGB scoring a timeout well above 10 minutes.
